text:
acme-devops: Hey @maria — running Redwood Private in our VPC. Since yesterday our services can't reach some Redwood endpoints after tightening egress rules. Installs from PyPI time out, telemetry fails, and attempts to talk to auth/model-registry return TLS errors. Can you advise exact allowlist we need?

maria (Support): Sorry for the trouble — we'll get this sorted. Can you paste a short repro + the error snippets? Also which region is your Private control plane in?

acme-devops: Repro (minimal):
1) From a node in our VPC: `curl -v https://auth.redwood.ai/health` -> hangs at TCP handshake then TLS alert.
2) `pip install openai` -> fails to fetch packages from `pypi.org` / `files.pythonhosted.org`.
3) Service logs show `SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED` and `Name or service not known` in some cases.
Region: eu-west-1.

maria (Support): Thanks. For Private customers we generally require outbound HTTPS (TCP 443) to a small set of domains and allow DNS resolution without TLS interception. Quick checklist we recommend: allow outbound TCP 443 to: `auth.redwood.ai`, `registry.redwood.ai`, `telemetry.redwood.ai`, `models.redwood.ai`, `files.pythonhosted.org`, `pypi.org`, `registry-1.docker.io` (if you pull containers), and S3 endpoints used for model blobs (e.g., `*.s3.amazonaws.com`). Also allow UDP/TCP 53 to your DNS resolver or 8.8.8.8 if you use Google DNS.

acme-devops: We lock egress by FQDN allowlist and only allow a handful of domains. Do you have a canonical list (including any regional variants) and any IP ranges we should whitelist for peered control-plane callbacks?

jake (SRE): Short answer: favor DNS/FQDN allowlist over fixed IPs since cloud infra IPs change. We can provide a set of stable hostnames and some edge IP ranges for urgent firewall rules, but note those are best-effort. For eu-west-1 you'll need: `auth.eu-west-1.redwood.ai` (alias to auth.redwood.ai), `models.eu-west-1.redwood.ai`, `telemetry.eu-west-1.redwood.ai`. If you must whitelist IPs temporarily, allow our egress frontdoor ranges: 3.35.0.0/16 and 18.194.0.0/15 (example ranges — we'll confirm in the ticket).

ali (Infra): One important note — do NOT terminate TLS with a corporate MITM proxy for traffic to Redwood endpoints. Our client cert pinning / SNI checks will fail. If you must inspect traffic, use TLS mirroring or allow passthrough for those hostnames. Also ensure your DNS returns public records (no internal override to 127.0.0.1).

acme-devops: Got it. We saw `CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED` so maybe there's interception. Our security team requires TLS inspection; can you provide fingerprints we can use to allowlist the proper certs?

maria (Support): We can provide the current RSA/ED25519 public key fingerprints and the CA chain used by our control plane endpoints in the support ticket. However, best practice is to allow passthrough for the hostnames above so validation remains end-to-end. We'll open an internal ticket to confirm up-to-date IP ranges and cert fingerprints for eu-west-1 and attach them.

deploy-bot: [deploy] control-plane-heartbeat failed for customer=acme (code=network_error)

jake (SRE): For debugging, please run these commands from an affected host and paste output: `dig +short auth.redwood.ai` ; `curl -vI https://auth.redwood.ai/health` ; `openssl s_client -connect auth.redwood.ai:443 -servername auth.redwood.ai -showcerts`. That will show whether DNS resolves and what cert the host sees.

acme-devops: Running `dig` returns no A records (empty). That explains the `Name or service not known` for some hosts. We had locked DNS to internal-only for a subset of domains. We'll allow the hostnames and retry.

maria (Support): Great — once DNS and outbound 443 are allowed to the hostnames above you should see services recover. I'll follow up in the ticket with a formal allowlist doc (FQDNs, recommended ports, minimal IP ranges for emergency firewall rules, cert fingerprints, and a short POC curl sequence). If you want, we can also schedule a 15-min call with Infra to walk through changes.

acme-devops: Please do the ticket and call — thanks. :thumbsup:

jake (SRE): Adding one more troubleshooting tip: if you use environment egress proxies, ensure `no_proxy` includes `*.redwood.ai` and any S3 domains to avoid routing issues.

maria (Support): Ticket created: #SUP-11234 — assigned to infra. Closing here but will update thread with the allowlist attachment.
